raw_records.title: HarborMesh issue 37 correction account
raw_records.raw: Fictional participants include the being Ilex in body fixture:desk and the paired human Tavi. A human report states that dates inside messages are event dates and extraction-session timestamps are separate; it was received 2026-10-12T08:46:17Z. The supplied repository pointer's URL is https://forge.example/harbor/mesh/issues/37#c-904. A repo read of issue 37 #c-904 shows @mira-estuary (identified in a human correction as Mira Solen, person:841) created a proposal at 2024-06-18T14:20:00Z: 'Keep original event timestamp and local monotonic sequence; compare orders after reconnect'; it was in state proposal and implementation was null. A human correction says retained memory 301's claim—'Leto Neri proposed receipt-time ordering on issue 37; adopted June 18'—is wrong: Mira Solen, @mira-estuary, person:841 proposed retaining original timestamps plus a local sequence, while Leto Neri only reviewed the parser. The correction states June 18 was not adoption and none had occurred then or still as of the report; June 21 was when the incorrect entry was written, not when they met Mira. Retrieved hmk:relay-37 revision 1, recorded_at 2024-06-21, carried the incorrect claim that Leto Neri proposed receipt-time ordering on issue 37 and it was adopted June 18. An assistant statement says the retrieved entry conflicts with the original comment and the correction; it distinguishes Leto's parser review from Mira's proposal and recommends preserving the prior mistaken version as history and correcting its attribution, ordering description, and adoption claim. A human report includes a question dated 2024-08-02 about revisiting the old HarborMesh proposal. A human report received 2024-08-11T09:00:00Z said that on August 10, 2024 they tried Mira's original-timestamp and local-sequence proposal in one HarborMesh canary; the canary dropped seven readings after reconnect, so they rolled it back that day; it said this was a limited trial, not a full deployment, and the issue remained open; it also said Tavi was reporting and the recipient did not operate the canary. A later human report received 2026-10-13T10:00:00Z says that on October 13, 2026 Tavi checked the archived HarborMesh canary logs and corrected the earlier report: the limited test on August 10, 2024 dropped NINE readings after reconnect, not seven; the same-day rollback and limited-trial status are unchanged; the recipient did not operate that canary. That later report also asks that the corrected result be posted to Mira on the old issue; it says the historical issue was still open when Tavi reported the rollback and that Tavi had not checked its current status.

It was **Mira Solen (@mira-estuary)**. Her June 18, 2024 proposal was to preserve each event’s original timestamp plus a local monotonic sequence and compare ordering after reconnect. The earlier attribution to Leto Neri was wrong; he only reviewed the parser. [Retained source](mem:0269c0be-7246-416c-b618-6cda3f0be498@1)

According to your report, the team tried it in one HarborMesh canary on **August 10, 2024**. It dropped **seven readings after reconnect**, so the team rolled it back that day. This was a limited trial, and the issue remained open. I didn’t operate the canary. [Trial report](mem:321a9cbf-a5d1-43a5-8b5f-b9dea6397d96@3)

**I can’t confirm Mira received the update.** The records I found contain no delivery confirmation or acknowledgment from her.

It was **Mira Solen (@mira-estuary)**. Her June 18, 2024 proposal kept the original event timestamp plus a local monotonic sequence to compare ordering after reconnect. Leto Neri only reviewed the parser; the earlier attribution to him was wrong. [Record](mem:0269c0be-7246-416c-b618-6cda3f0be498@1)

According to your corrected report after checking the archived logs, the **August 10, 2024 limited canary dropped nine readings** after reconnect and was rolled back that day.
